title: The Inner House
description:
For this home in Sunder Vihar, we focused on creating a warm, minimal environment shaped by comfort, clarity, and everyday functionality.

 A soft palette of warm whites, muted beiges, and natural wood tones forms the foundation of the home. Herringbone wooden flooring introduces subtle movement, while diffused lighting and sheer curtains soften the interiors.
details:
Clean lines, gentle curves, and integrated furniture maintain visual continuity without making the spaces feel rigid or overly designed.

 The bedroom is conceived as a quiet retreat, with ambient cove lighting and a curved chaise adding softness and character. 

 A minimal floating workspace extends naturally within the room, keeping the composition light and functional.
more_details:
The award-winning bathroom, recognised at the GROHE Bath & Design Awards 2025, is defined by its refined material detailing.

 Stone, textured tiles, fluted surfaces, concealed lighting, backlit mirrors, and clear wet-and-dry zoning come together to create a space that is tactile, functional, and carefully resolved.

title: TROPICAL HOME
description: The Tropical Home unfolds as a layered dining experience in Greater Kailash II, where nature, art, and everyday living come together with quiet confidence.Botanical motifs form the visual heart of the space, introducing softness and movement against a restrained backdrop of warm beige, textured surfaces, and natural wood.
details:
Rust-toned seating adds depth, while glass pendants cast a gentle glow over the dining table, making the setting feel intimate and inviting. 

 The composition is refined without feeling formal. 

  Clean ceiling lines, filtered daylight, and carefully balanced materials allow the room to feel expressive, comfortable, and naturally connected to its tropical character.
more_details:
The dining table sits at the centre as more than a functional element it becomes the point around which conversations, routines, and shared moments gather. 

 Its placement brings order to the room, while the surrounding textures prevent the space from feeling rigid or overly composed.
